reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Grading during spinal shock without reassessment.
Treating Frankel and AIS grades as interchangeable.
name: Frankel Classification

version.label: Frankel grade (Frankel et al. 1969)
version.detail: Grades A–E. Superseded for standard classification by the ASIA Impairment Scale (ISNCSCI), which is not implemented pending review.

purpose: Simple grading of neurological function below a spinal cord injury.

calculatorNotice.title: Historical classification
calculatorNotice.message: The ASIA Impairment Scale (ISNCSCI) is the current standard. Frankel grades are still used in older literature and some scores, such as Tokuhashi.

options.label: A: Complete
options.detail: No motor or sensory function below the level.

options.label: B: Sensory only
options.detail: Some sensation preserved; no motor function below the level.

options.label: C: Motor useless
options.detail: Some motor function preserved, of no practical use.

options.label: D: Motor useful
options.detail: Useful motor function below the level.

options.label: E: Recovery
options.detail: Normal motor and sensory function; abnormal reflexes may persist.

resultStates.label: Grade A: complete
resultStates.summary: No motor or sensory function below the level.
resultStates.detail: Assess for spinal shock; reassess serially according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade B: sensory only
resultStates.summary: Sensory but no motor function below the level.
resultStates.detail: Reassess serially according to local protocol.

resultStates.label: Grade C: motor useless
resultStates.summary: Some motor function, not of practical use.

resultStates.label: Grade D: motor useful
resultStates.summary: Useful motor function below the level.

resultStates.label: Grade E: recovery
resultStates.summary: Normal motor and sensory function at this assessment.

clinicalContext.text: The first widely used spinal cord injury grading system.

clinicalInsights.text: Report the neurological level alongside the grade.

limitations.text: 'Motor useful' and 'motor useless' are not precisely defined, so grading is subjective.

limitations: Does not define the neurological level or sacral sparing.

confounders.effect: Can make an incomplete injury appear complete.

guideSections.what: A five-grade (A–E) classification of function below a spinal cord injury.
guideSections.whenToUse: Where Frankel grading is required, e.g. older protocols or scores.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess motor and sensory function below the level and choose the grade.

sources.citation: Frankel HL, Hancock DO, Hyslop G, et al. The value of postural reduction in the initial management of closed injuries of the spine with paraplegia and tetraplegia. Paraplegia. 1969;7(3):179-192.
